Properties.Ultimate Tensile Strength: Below that of MG and CG materials

Yield Strength.FG material at 873 K: About one third that of FG, actual value not mentioned

Additional Information: The yield strength of the materials follows the Hall-Petch relationship, with a strong increase in ry upon refining the grain size from 155 to 4.4 lm at all temperatures up to 873 K.
Material tested at temperatures up to 873 K. Maximum tensile strength and yield strength occur at liquid nitrogen temperature. Strengths decrease with increasing temperature.
Testing temperatures: 293 K, 473 K, 1073 K. FG material shows unique yield-point phenomena and maximum tensile strength behavior at high temperature.

The temperature dependence of the yield stress at low temperatures is not significantly influenced by grain size. The yield strength vs. temperature curves are roughly parallel up to intermediate temperatures.

In pure fcc metals, the thermal contribution (rth) to yield strength is usually negligible and temperature-independent. In binary Cu-based solid solution alloys (Cu-Al, Cu-Ge or Cu-Mn), rth increases with increasing solute content, shifting the critical temperature for temperature-dependent to temperature-independent yield strength to higher values.
